attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-03-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
She presents to clinic with one week of yellowing of the skin and sclerae.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 59-year-old female with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypothyroidism, obesity, and prior incisional hernia presents with one week of yellowing of skin and sclerae. She also notes her stools have become pale and her urine has turned unusually dark. She denies fever, abdominal pain, or nausea. Her appetite is normal, and she reports regular bowel movements. She recovered well initially but began to notice progressive discoloration of her eyes and urine three days ago.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Incisional hernia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Hypertension
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Dyslipidemia
- Hypothyroidism
- Obesity (BMI 33)

She has no prior history of liver disease,.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
The patient underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy eight days ago for presumed symptomatic gallstones. Her surgical records indicate that no intraoperative cholangiography was performed.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily
- Levothyroxine 75 mcg PO daily
- Aspirin 81 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension
- Father: Coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia
- Sister: Cholecystectomy for cholelithiasis
- Brother: Inguinal hernia repair

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Alcohol use, or intravenous drug use.

VITAL SIGNS:
Her vital signs are normal, and she remains afebrile.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical exam reveals scleral icterus and mild jaundice of the skin. There is no abdominal tenderness or hepatosplenomegaly. Surgical wounds are clean and healing well. Bowel sounds are present, and the abdomen is soft and nondistended. Rectal exam is deferred. The rest of her exam is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory results are pending.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: General Surgery
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
She comes to the clinic for evaluation of a bulge in her lower abdomen.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She first noticed the swelling about six months ago, and it has gradually increased in size. The mass becomes more noticeable when she stands for prolonged periods or performs physical activity, and it tends to reduce or disappear when she lies down. She denies nausea, vomiting, constipation, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Hypertension
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Dyslipidemia
- Hypothyroidism
- Obesity (BMI 33)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
Her medical history includes a laparotomy performed five years ago for small bowel obstruction, and she has not had any subsequent abdominal surgeries or trauma.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily
- Levothyroxine 75 mcg PO daily
- Aspirin 81 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension
- Father: Coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia
- Sister: Cholecystectomy for cholelithiasis
- Brother: Inguinal hernia repair

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Denies alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, there is a soft, non-tender, reducible mass located along the old surgical scar in the lower midline abdomen. The swelling becomes more prominent with Valsalva maneuver and is not associated with overlying erythema or warmth. No other abdominal or groin masses are palpated.
